notes: Units were aligned by anchor/sentence overlap. Stance agreed on all 12 documents. MAIN PATTERN 1, modality of imperatives in advisory guideline lists (most of the modality disagreements): CS 1301/1332 'Guidelines for Ethical AI Use' and CS 2050 'heuristics' are introduced as guidance ('deviating does not automatically mean misconduct'). Coder A used should/should-not for some imperatives; Coder B used must/must-not. Resolved to must/must-not for imperative wording ('Use AI for learning, not for writing', 'write your response in your own words', 'close the tool', 'Avoid AI tools that auto-generate code', 'Never hit Copy', 'do not copy back', 'Do not have ... open at the same time'). Both coders had already coded the undisputed 'Do not copy and paste' / 'Do NOT work ... simultaneously' as must-not, and Coder A's own notes state this rule. The advisory status is captured by the separate 'Deviating ... does not automatically mean misconduct' units. Non-imperative phrasings ('Treat your AI interaction as...', 'avoiding using AI directly integrated') keep the agreed should/should-not. PATTERN 2, consequence statements: 'Submitting content generated by AI tools will be treated as academic misconduct' and 'Copying solutions from ... AI ... is considered plagiarism' resolved to informs (A had must-not): they state a consequence, and the underlying prohibition is coded in its own units. 'Citation does not create an exception to this rule' -> informs. 'Generative AI is an excellent resource for testing your knowledge...' (CS 1331) and 'AI assistants like ChatGPT can be a great resource' (CSE 6040) -> informs, not may: they describe and do not grant permission. CS 3510 'you will NOT have access to any of this material on the exams' -> informs; the next sentence ('IS considered cheating to use any outside resource on an exam') -> must-not, P22. PATTERN 3, phase/actor on analogies and rationale: analogy units (AI use 'similar to collaborating with peers', 'equivalent to someone else writing your assignment', 'just as you should not let a classmate write your solutions') resolved to phase general (A), since they frame rather than regulate a phase. The OMSCS 'same academic integrity policy applies to AI assistance' and the 'cost of overreliance' rationale -> actor student (B), because the syllabus addresses students. CTL's warnings about students overusing or avoiding AI without a syllabus statement -> instructor/course-start (A), because they are reasons given to instructors. OIT 'examine the handbooks' -> general; OIT vendor risk evaluation -> actor all (it binds anyone acquiring tools). PATTERN 4, policy_type: OMSCS 'consult with AI agents just as you would ... discuss ideas' -> P15 (A) over P12; 'encouraged to let AI assistants aid in developing your understanding' -> P12 (B) over P02. 'all code must be your own' / 'when should students submit their own individual work' -> P29 over P19. OIT 'mindful engagement' -> P56 (P32 is about the student as problem-solver). OIT educational-content use -> P56 (descriptive, not a P48 rule about instructors' materials). CTL citation style (APA/Chicago/MLA) -> P25. CS 3790 cite-each-section -> P24 (P27 is code-specific). CSE 6040 exam intent -> P22/student. CTL 'Copilot or other approved systems' -> P50/student (approved/vetted tools). PATTERN 5, merged vs split units: OIT 'Key aspects to consider' sentence was merged by A and split by B into security/privacy (P50), legal/copyright (P52), integrity (P56). Kept B's split. Only-A units kept: OIT phishing best-practice directive, OIT 'Review Content Before Publishing' directive, CS 6750 'must be obvious what portion is your own creation', the CS 6750/7637 rule against copying exam content into any tool (kept as P49; generic 'any tool' in an open-book context, flagged here as AI-implicit), CSE 6040 'write up your own notebooks' (modality set to should, the literal wording) and 'taking shortcuts only hurts you' (retyped P41), ECE 2035 'design, write, and debug individually'. Dropped only-A: the grammar-checker permission in CS 6750/7637/CSE 6040, because it is inferred from 'disable anything more advanced than a grammar checker' and not stated. Only-B units kept: the 'hand your device to someone else' analogy (P45/general), 'prohibited from having these tools directly integrated into your workspace' (a distinct sentence, not an exact repeat), CSE 6040 'You may use Google, Bing' on exams (P07, matching the agreed Google Overview carve-out), CTL 'This misunderstanding can lead students...', CS 1301/1332 'guidelines are designed to help you stay within integrity boundaries', CS 1331 'assignments provide opportunities to learn', CS 3790 'you must do both of the following' lead-in. Dropped only-B: CS 2050 'following these heuristics essentially guarantees...', which is the second clause of the same sentence A coded as one unit.
